episodes.196250: Late afternoon and evening rainfall on September 9th, associated with outer bands from approaching Tropical Storm Francine, saturated the ground from Brownsville to South Padre Island.  A Persistent band formed toward daybreak on the 10th and persisted through mid morning, dropping additional heavy rainfall. Total rainfall from the entire episode ranged from 5 to nearly 8 inches, with an estimated 3 to 5 inches falling during the early to mid morning of September 10th.  Urban flooding was noted in parts of southeast Cameron County.
episodes.196262: A surface front was stalled across north-central FL as high pressure across the mid-Atlantic area shifted southward. Breezy onshore winds and above normal moisture continued to bring waves of heavy coastal showers.
episodes.196412: Severe thunderstorm wind gusts occurred at Sterling in Burleigh County. Multiple trees were damaged in the community, with estimated wind gusts of 75 mph.
episodes.196431: A potent shortwave trough/Mesoscale Convective Vortex tracked southeast across the area, causing showers and thunderstorms for much of the Buffalo forecast area. A few of the thunderstorms became severe with tornado and wind damage, along with rain that was heavy enough to cause Flash Flooding issues.
episodes.196473: A frontal boundary stalled over Central Florida brought a warm and very moist airmass over South Florida, which combined with ample lift from mid-level troughing to develop widespread slow-moving showers and thunderstorms over the area during the afternoon and evening.
episodes.196662: An upper level trough lingered in the region, promoting unsettled weather conditions. Additionally, a tropical wave approached, bringing plenty of moisture in the region. Widespread showers and thunderstorms were observed across Puerto Rico, with rainfall accumulations of 1 to 3 inches each day, and maximum amounts up to 5 inches. This led to several reports of mudslides, lightning, and flooding.
episodes.197033: TS Bebinca originated in the Federated States of Micronesia near Pohnpei and Kosrae as a surface trough. Bebinca gradually consolidated into a closed low-level circulation as it moved WNW past Pohnpei and Chuuk as was monitored as Invest 95W. The Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) issued its first warning on TD 14W as it sat about 200 miles SE of Guam on 10 Sep. It was briefly elevated to a 40 mph TS as it passed to the west of southern Guam early morning on the 11th. Rainfall was the more notable hazard with Guam seeing the bulk of rainfall. Heavy rains were less prevalent across the CNMI, but Saipan did see some erosion and runoff due to all the loose soil and gravel from large stretches of road work. Little wind damage was reported beyond some downed limbs and fleshier vegetations such as banana and papaya trees.

events.narrative: Large tree branch downed at intersection of Alleghany Road and Akron Road. Trees also downed on Akron Road, Little Falls Road, and Phelps Road.

NWS Storm Survey confirms brief, weak EF-0 tornado in the Hamlet of Indian Falls from near NY Route 77 to Little Falls Road. About a half dozen trees were damaged or blown down, but all trees showed significant rot. Max winds were 75 mph, path length was 0.2 miles, width 50 yards, and duration was 2 minutes.
A public rain gauge located along the Nassau |            River just west of Amelia Island measured 3.14 inches storm total rainfalll.
Multiple trees were damaged in the city of Sterling.

There were several reports of flash flooding in the city of Brownsville, mainly bracketed by Price Road and Expressway IH-69E on the west, Price Road and State Highway 48 on the east, extending to the Southmost neighborhood on the south side of the city. Reports included: Multiple intersections along Boca Chica Blvd impassable due to flooded roadways between McDavitt Blvd and  Kings Hwy and Boca Chica was nearly impassable, as well as the intersection known as Four Corners at State Highway 4; flooding extending along State Highway 4 to Southmost Blvd., and flooding along and near the frontage road at Price Road and IH-69E, extending to Barnard Road, and to nearby apartment complexes and shopping centers in this area.||While all locations inside the ascribed polygon may not have reached flash flood levels - 3 feet or higher of ponded water - the reports of impassible roads and photographic evidence suggesting pockets of this level of water depth made the case for a flash flood event in these areas.||Damage to any property was unknown as of this writing.
There was an undetermined amount of water flowing over State Highway 4 near Boca Chica Village and the SpaceX/Starbase area during the early morning hours.
Cameron County Parks Department reported photographic evidence of 1 to 2 feet of standing water along Park Road 100 north of the City of South Padre Island during the morning of September 10th.

Emergency Managers provided several photos of flood waters on Padre Blvd extending as far north as the intersection of Padre Blvd and Dolphin Street.  Poor drainage in the area likely contributed to water depth between 2 and 3 feet along the highway.  Damage was unknown as of this writing.
Roadways were flooded on Ruben M Torres Blvd near N Central Avenue with an estimated 1 to 2 feet of water depth in spots.

Flooding occurred in the usual places during heavy rainfall as Tropical Storm Bebinca passed near Guam: Polaris Point/Route 1 in Sumay-Piti corridor and other common urban flood areas. Most of Guam saw 24 hour rainfall (2200ChST on September 10th to 2200ChST on September 11th) of between 5 and 7.50 inches, as reported by COOP, CoCoRaHS, USGS and ASOS stations across the island. According the automated gauges, most of the rain fell from 0200ChST to 1200ChST on September 11th. The weather office did not receive many reports of damaged or stalled vehicles due to flooded roads, so damage estimates were kept at 0 (zero) $USD.

At Saipan, there were problems with runoff due to heavy showers as Tropical Storm Bebinca passed near Guam, resulting in considerable erosion of gravel roads. Much of the highway/street infrastructure along western Saipan is under construction, with exposed gravel and dirt in many areas from San Antonio northward to Garapan. Saipan International Airport recorded a 24 hour rainfall of 1.49 inches (2200ChST September 10th to 2200ChST September 11th).

Broadcast media reported via social media partial flooding on PR-1 near Milla de Oro, close to MCS, directly in front of Boveda Restaurante. Some lanes were impassable, but vehicles were still able to pass through the available lane, albeit with some difficulty.
A 911 reporter informed that Calle 88 in Carolina is being affected by flooding.
A stranded car due to flooding was reported in Calle Junin, Intersection with Calle 1.
An NWS employee reported heavy traffic at Ave Iturregui, in the traffic light in front of Ciudad Deportiva, due to flood waters making the road almost impassable.
Adjuntas. Adjuntas OMME Director reported a creek out of its banks in Barrio Tanama Sector Valle along PR-526 in Adjuntas near Barra El Valle.
Broadcast media reported flooding along Avenue Luis Munoz Rivera, right in front of El Hipopotamo restaurant. The road looked almost impassable with cars crossing with difficulty.
Fajardo OMME Director informed of a water surge from Rio Fajardo, flooding PR-194 near Iglesia Bautista Nueva Jerusalem. The road was closed due to water overpassing the bridge.
A car was stranded at PR-114 as flooding waters from Rio Guanajibo continued to cover the road.

Social media posts contained pictures and videos of street flooding with 6 inches of standing water near Collins Avenue and Northeast 23rd Street in Miami Beach after rounds of showers and thunderstorms moved through the area. Rainfall estimates in the area were 3 to 4 inches in a 3 hour timeframe.
